questions.text: An operator delete(i) for a binary heap data structure is to be designed to delete the item in the i-th node.Assume that the heap is implemented in an array and i refers to the i-th index of thearray.If the heap tree has depth d (number of edges on the path from the root to the farthest leaf),the n what is the time complexity to re-fix the heap efficiently after the removal of the element?
questions.solution:
To delete node i: move the last element into position i, then either sift it up or down. Either way it moves along one root-to-leaf path, at most d levels [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(d)[/latex]. It can take that long, so it is not [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: O(d) but not O(1)

questions.text: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?
questions.solution:
Use a circular array with front and rear indices: ENQUEUE writes at rear and moves it, DEQUEUE reads at front and moves it (both modulo the array size). No shifting is needed, so both are [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time

options: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time

At most one operation can be performed in O(1) time but the worst case time for
the other operation will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
The worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](n)
Worst case time complexity for both operations will be [latex]\Omega[/latex](logn)

questions.text: If a node has [latex]K[/latex] children in B tree, then the node contains exactly _____ keys.
questions.solution:
In a B-tree, a node with K child pointers holds exactly K [latex]-[/latex] 1 keys, which separate the children.

Answer: K [latex]-[/latex] 1

questions.text: The queue data structure is to be realized by using stack. The number of stacks needed would be
questions.solution:
Use one stack for enqueue and one for dequeue. When the dequeue stack is empty, pop everything from the first stack into it, which reverses the order to FIFO.

Answer: 2 stacks

questions.text: A hash table with ten buckets with one slot per bucket is shown in the following figure. The symbols S1 to S7 initially entered using a hashing function with linear probing. The maximum number of comparisons needed in searching an item that is not present is
questions.solution:
An unsuccessful search stops at the first empty slot. Empty slots are 2, 5 and 7.

The longest run is for a key that hashes to slot 8: check 8, 9, 0, 1, then the empty slot 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 comparisons.

Answer: 5
